chooseAdventureSubtitle: SpArki, the blue robotic teddy-bear teacher, has two paths for Age 5–11 explorers. Pick one to begin.

ai-coding.title: AI, Coding & Software Adventures
ai-coding.description: Join SpArki to learn what AI is, how code works, and how software helps people.

social-safety.title: Social Media Safety & Kindness
social-safety.description: SpArki helps you practice safe watching, kind comments, and healthy screen time.

ai-1-what-is-ai.title: What Is AI?
ai-1-what-is-ai.summary: SpArki shows how AI can sort and draw by learning from examples instead of magic.
contentBlocks: Story: SpArki helps sort toys into boxes using examples.
Idea: AI learns from patterns in examples, not from magic.
Pause: Look around the room and find 3 things you could sort.

activity.title: Design Your Own AI Helper
activity.description: Draw your own AI helper and label what it sorts for you (toys, snacks, books, or something else).

quizQuestions.prompt: AI learns from…
SpArki uses AI to help…
A pattern is something that…

thinkPrompts.label: Think about this!
thinkPrompts.text: Look around the room. Can you find 3 things you could sort into groups? (e.g. toys, books, crayons)

thinkPrompts.label: Think about this!
thinkPrompts.text: SpArki learns from examples, not magic. What is one example you could show a friend so they learn something new?

ai-2-coding-games.title: Coding as Games
ai-2-coding-games.summary: SpArki turns code into silly "if this, then that" games you can act out with your body.
contentBlocks: Game: If I clap, you jump. If I stomp, you spin—this is like an if/then rule.
Idea: Code is a list of instructions the computer follows exactly.

activity.title: Act Out Algorithms
activity.description: Create a short "algorithm" for a classmate to follow (like getting from the door to a chair).

quizQuestions.prompt: Code is like…
options: A recipe or set of rules
A secret language only robots know

quizQuestions.prompt: If the code says "if it rains, open umbrella", the umbrella opens when…

ai-3-software-explorers.title: Software Explorers
ai-3-software-explorers.summary: Kids explore what "software" means by looking at apps, games, and tools they already use.
contentBlocks: Examples: drawing apps, math games, video chat.
Idea: software is instructions that live inside devices.

activity.title: Software Scavenger Hunt
activity.description: With a grown-up, find 3 examples of helpful software at home or at school and draw them.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which is software?
Software lives inside…

ai-4-ai-in-the-world.title: AI in Our World
ai-4-ai-in-the-world.summary: SpArki shows friendly examples of AI in schools, farms, and hospitals, and talks about when AI might be wrong.
contentBlocks: Story: AI helps sort mail, suggest songs, and translate languages.
Pause: Think of one place you have seen AI (even if you did not know it yet).

activity.title: AI Around Us
activity.description: Make a simple "AI map" of your school or home—mark where AI might live (like in tablets, speakers, or cars).

quizQuestions.prompt: AI can help people by…

ai-5-ethical-coding.title: Kind & Fair Coding
ai-5-ethical-coding.summary: Kids talk about fairness, kindness, and how humans are responsible for how AI is used.
contentBlocks: Scenario: a game that only shows some kids as heroes.
Idea: we can change the rules to be more fair and kind.

activity.title: Fix the Story
activity.description: Work with a grown-up to change a short "unfair" story into a kinder, more fair version.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who is responsible for how AI behaves?
options: The people who design and use it

safety-instagram.title: Staying Safe on Instagram
safety-instagram.summary: SpArki shows how to share photos safely, keep your account private, and always ask a grown-up first.
contentBlocks: Story: A classmate wants to post a photo of the whole class. SpArki helps them ask a grown-up before sharing.
Rule: Keep your account private so only people you and a grown-up know can follow you.
Rule: Never put your full name, school, or address in your bio.
Pause: Think of one grown-up you can ask if you see a strange message online.

activity.title: Design a Safe Profile
activity.description: Draw a pretend profile page that shows fun things (like pets or hobbies) but no private info. Share it with a grown-up.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who should you ask before posting a picture online?
What should your account settings be?
options: Private to people you and a grown-up know

quizQuestions.prompt: Which information should you keep off your profile?
If a stranger sends you a message, what do you do?
options: Reply and make a new friend
Ignore, block, and tell a grown-up

quizQuestions.prompt: Who decides what you can post?
options: You and a trusted grown-up together

thinkPrompts.label: Think about this!
thinkPrompts.text: Who is one grown-up you could ask before posting a photo? Talk to them about it!

thinkPrompts.label: Think about this!
thinkPrompts.text: What would you never put in your profile? (Hint: school name, address, phone number)

safety-tiktok.title: Kind & Safe TikTok
safety-tiktok.summary: SpArki explains how to keep videos private, turn off strangers, and handle mean comments kindly and safely.
contentBlocks: Rule: Only post videos with a grown-up's permission.
Safety: Turn off "everyone" so only friends you and a grown-up know can see your videos.
Kindness: You never have to reply to mean comments. It is okay to block and report.
Pause: Practice what you would say to a grown-up if you see something that feels yucky online.

activity.title: Kind Comment Practice
activity.description: With a grown-up, write 3 kind comments you could leave on someone's video that are safe and encouraging.

quizQuestions.prompt: Before posting a video, you should…
Who should be able to see your videos?
options: Only people you and a grown-up know

quizQuestions.prompt: If someone leaves a mean comment, you can…
options: Block, report, and tell a grown-up

quizQuestions.prompt: What information should stay private?
When something online feels wrong, you should…
options: Tell a trusted grown-up right away

safety-snapchat.title: Snaps, Streaks & Safety
safety-snapchat.summary: SpArki teaches that snaps do not really "disappear" and that streaks are never more important than feelings or safety.
contentBlocks: Myth-buster: Snaps can be screenshotted or saved, so treat them like any other picture.
Rule: Never send pictures you would not want a teacher or grown-up to see.
Feelings: It is okay to break a streak if you need a break or feel uncomfortable.
Pause: Think of one safe snap you could send, like a pet or a drawing.

activity.title: Safe Snap Ideas
activity.description: Draw or list 5 silly but safe snap ideas you could share with friends, then check them with a grown-up.

quizQuestions.prompt: Do snaps always disappear forever?
options: No, they can be saved or screenshotted

quizQuestions.prompt: What is a safe kind of picture to send?
options: Your pet wearing a silly hat

quizQuestions.prompt: If someone asks for a picture that feels wrong, you should…
options: Say no and tell a grown-up

quizQuestions.prompt: Streaks are…
options: Fun, but never more important than feelings or safety

quizQuestions.prompt: Who can help you decide what is okay to send?

safety-roblox.title: Safe Play on Roblox
safety-roblox.summary: SpArki shows how to use chat filters, block strangers, and never share private info while playing games.
contentBlocks: Rule: Use in-game safety settings and let a grown-up help set them up.
Safety: Never share your real name, age, school, or address in chat.
Boundary: You never have to join voice chat or private games with strangers.
Pause: Practice what you would do if someone in a game makes you feel weird or scared.

activity.title: Family Game Rules
activity.description: With your grown-up, write 3 simple family rules for playing games safely online.

quizQuestions.prompt: What is okay to share in game chat?
options: A nickname that does not reveal private info

quizQuestions.prompt: If a stranger invites you to a private game, you should…
options: Say no, leave, and tell a grown-up

quizQuestions.prompt: Who should help set your safety settings?
If someone is mean in chat, you can…
options: Block, report, and take a break

quizQuestions.prompt: Games should make you feel…

safety-fortnite.title: Fortnite & Voice Chat Boundaries
safety-fortnite.summary: SpArki explains how to mute, block, and set kind rules for talking to others in fast-paced games.
contentBlocks: Rule: Only use voice chat with people you and a grown-up know.
Safety: You can mute or leave any time a conversation feels bad.
Kindness: Teasing that hurts is not okay, even if it is "just a game."
Pause: Practice a sentence you could say to a grown-up if someone is yelling at you in a game.

activity.title: Voice Chat Plan
activity.description: With a grown-up, create a short plan for when you will mute, leave, or take a break from voice chat.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who is it safest to talk with in voice chat?
options: People you and a grown-up know

quizQuestions.prompt: If someone is yelling or being mean, you can…
options: Mute or leave and tell a grown-up

quizQuestions.prompt: Is it okay to tease if someone is upset?
options: No, we should be kind even in games

quizQuestions.prompt: Private info you should never share in voice chat includes…
Who can you talk to if a game makes you feel upset?

safety-reddit.title: Reading Safely on Reddit & Forums
safety-reddit.summary: SpArki talks about how posts and comments are not always true, and how to avoid grown-up spaces and scary content.
contentBlocks: Idea: Anyone can post online, so not everything you read is true or kind.
Rule: Stick to kid-friendly spaces a grown-up has checked first.
Safety: Never click strange links or messages that promise prizes.
Pause: Practice saying "Can you check this with me?" to a grown-up when you are unsure.

activity.title: Healthy Online Spaces
activity.description: Together with a grown-up, make a list of websites and apps that are "green light" safe for you right now.

quizQuestions.prompt: Are all posts and comments on the internet true?
options: Only if they have many likes

quizQuestions.prompt: Where should you spend time online?
options: Kid-friendly spaces a grown-up has checked

quizQuestions.prompt: If you see a scary or confusing post, you should…
options: Show a trusted grown-up and talk about it

quizQuestions.prompt: Links that promise prizes or money are often…
When something online feels "off", a good first step is to…
